Our home court is Svanemøllehallen on Østerbro. Academy players train up to five days a week, Monday to Friday, play league games most weekends and travel abroad every year.

Talata Academy

Academy players are on court most weekday afternoons and play games on the weekend. That is DBBF league games in Denmark, plus EYBL international stages in Europe. We confirm host cities stage by stage. Over a season it comes to 30+ games, in Denmark, Lithuania, Sweden and more.

We sit down and watch film, so players understand what they did instead of repeating it blind. Mental training is part of the week too.

Basketball is how we prepare kids for whatever comes next. That means discipline, teamwork, showing up when it is hard, and handling wins and losses. Academy alumni have gone on to play abroad, and the connections are there for players who earn them.

Alumni

Malthe Mikkelsen committed to Orangeville Prep in Canada at 15.

He started 2025/26 at Fort Erie International Academy in Ontario and finished it at Orangeville Prep, one of the top prep programs in North America. Talata ran his move. How our placement works.

Johan Lyager Joensen left for Ohio at 15.

Johan was on the floor in the first season, when Talata was twenty kids and one team. This year he plays for the Purple Riders at Martins Ferry High School. American high school is the most common route into the NCAA. His family ran the move, and his two years in this gym got him ready for it.

Valdemar Scharfe went to New Jersey this fall.

Valdemar trained at our camps and in the Academy, then played for Talata Men. This fall he trains with The Patrick School basketball program in New Jersey. Talata set the move up with him.

Coaches

Four coaches work with Academy players every week.

Captained Mount Royal University in Calgary and played pro in Canada, Lithuania and Denmark. Coached in Canada, Lithuania, Indonesia and Denmark.

Prices

3.300 kr per half-season, paid twice a year. It covers the season at home:

  • Team training up to five days a week, Monday to Friday
  • Film and video review
  • Mental training
  • A practice jersey to borrow
  • DBBF licence, gym rental and referees
  • Coaching from Deng, Jordan and Georg

We played our first EYBL stage in Budapest in 2024. Travel to stages is billed per trip. We confirm dates, destinations and costs before anyone commits, so you can plan.

Questions

What does Academy cost, and what is included?

3.300 kr per half season, one price for every player. It covers all training, strength training, mental training and a jersey to borrow for games.

Is it cheaper if my child trains fewer days?

One price covers the full week, up to five sessions. Coming fewer days keeps the same fee.

Which team fits my child's age?

Academy follows the Danish federation, which goes on your age on 1 October. A player still under 15 on 1 October plays U15, and the same goes for U13, U17 and U19. Send the date of birth when you book and we place your child.

We are new. Which session do we come to first?

A 13 or 14-year-old who played in a club before starts with U13 Academy, Monday at Strandvejsskolen or Friday at Bellahøj Hallerne. A beginner that age starts with Junior on Tuesday or Thursday. U17 players come Wednesday at Kulturhuset Indre By or Friday at Bellahøj Hallerne. U19 players come Monday at Svanemøllehallen or Friday at Nørre Fælled Skole. Girls 15 and up train with the Stevnsgade girls team.

Can we get help with the fee?

Yes, case by case. The board can approve financial support for a family. Write to us and we look at it together.

Why do I only see one team in Holdsport?

New players start on our general Talata Basketball team in Holdsport. We move them to their age team once age and program are settled.

Book a trial

Your first session is free. Places are limited. Tell us about your player and we set up a trial session to see them on court. You see the day, time and gym as soon as you send this, and we email it too.

Age groups run from 1 October, so the date decides the team.
